items.title: Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando Are Married
items.summary:
Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando are married. The couple wed Saturday in Palm Springs, California, and Cyrus confirmed it herself the following day with a set of wedding photos on Instagram, captioned "M + M" alongside a white heart emoji and the date 11.21.26.

The Hollywood Reporter, citing Entertainment Tonight, placed the ceremony in Palm Springs, after TMZ first reported that Cyrus, 33, and Morando, 28, were expected to marry over the weekend. Cyrus' stepsister Lily-Rose Purcell had already offered a preview on her Instagram Stories on Friday, posting images from the rehearsal dinner that showed tables set with crimson flowers and a menu printed with the couple's initials.

Cyrus and Morando, a musician himself, met on a blind date in 2021, a detail she shared with British Vogue in 2023. Their relationship has also been a working one: Morando collaborated with her on the albums "Endless Summer Vacation" and "Something Beautiful."

The engagement surfaced in December 2025, when Cyrus appeared alongside Morando at the premiere of "Avatar: Fire and Ash" — a film she contributed the song "Dream as One" to — wearing a gold band on her left ring finger. People confirmed the engagement a day later. Us Weekly reported more than two weeks after that the pair had discussed eloping rather than staging a traditional wedding, with a source telling the outlet, "Miley is really happy right now and in such a good, calm place. She's not super into the idea of doing another wedding."

The reference to "another wedding" points to Cyrus' first. She married actor Liam Hemsworth in 2018, a decade after the two met on the set of the 2010 Nicholas Sparks adaptation "The Last Song," and the couple divorced in 2020 after a long on-again, off-again relationship.

items.title: Sheila Mangubat Dies: ’90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days’ Star Was 35
items.summary:
Sheila Mangubat, who appeared on the sixth season of TLC's "90 Day Fiancé: Before the 90 Days," has died at 35. David Dangerfield, the man she dated on the series, announced the death on Instagram, saying she died Saturday in the Philippines.

"It breaks my heart to share the news from her family that Sheila passed away on Saturday in the Philippines," Dangerfield wrote in the post, as reported by Deadline. "I am devastated and still trying to process this loss. Please keep her son, her family, and me in your prayers. Thank you for all your love and support." No cause was given.

Mangubat and Dangerfield joined the franchise in 2023, having met through an online sign language group. Their relationship drew attention in part because of how they communicated: Mangubat was hard of hearing and Dangerfield is deaf, and the two spoke primarily in ASL.

Their season followed Dangerfield to the Philippines, where Mangubat lived with her mother, her father and her son, Jhonreil. The season closed with Mangubat accepting his proposal.

items.title: Tom Jackson, Denver Broncos’ All-Pro Linebacker and ESPN Analyst, Dies at 75
items.summary:
Tom Jackson, the Denver Broncos linebacker who spent 14 seasons anchoring the team's "Orange Crush" defense before becoming one of ESPN's most recognizable football analysts, died Friday at 75. His family informed the network of his death, which was announced without a stated cause.

Born in Cleveland on April 4, 1951, Jackson was recruited out of John Adams High School by University of Louisville coach Lee Corso, a future ESPN colleague. Denver took him in the fourth round of the 1973 draft, 88th overall, and he played his entire career there: 191 regular-season games, a franchise record when he retired in 1986, plus 10 playoff appearances. He was a first-team All-Pro in 1977 and 1978, a three-time Pro Bowl selection, a member of the Broncos' first Super Bowl team and, at 36, the oldest linebacker in the league when he stepped away.

Jackson moved into broadcasting almost immediately, co-hosting a Broncos program on Denver's KCNC-TV and a postgame show on KUSA-TV, along with a syndicated daily radio commentary show. ESPN hired him in 1987, and he spent three decades there, most visibly beside Chris Berman on "NFL Primetime" and "Sunday NFL Countdown." He won a Sports Emmy in 2009, received the Pro Football Hall of Fame's Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award in 2015 and retired from broadcasting the following year, returning once in 2019 for a digital edition of "NFL Primetime" with Berman.

Berman, according to The Hollywood Reporter, said he had spoken with Jackson at length on Tuesday and called the death unexpected. "All of us are stunned," he said in a statement. "We've lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years." ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro said Jackson "brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans."

The Broncos, who inducted Jackson into their Ring of Fame in 1992, described him in a statement as "an inspirational leader and fierce competitor" who "carried himself with class, warmth and humility" away from the field. ESPN's NFL studio carries his name alongside Berman's. Jackson, who often said he had been "blessed to work for two companies in my life: the Denver Broncos and ESPN," is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and daughters Taylor and Morgan; another daughter, Andrea, died in 1997 at age 9 from injuries in a car accident.
